headline: Single-cell and spatial profiling links T and B cell states to immunotherapy response
label: Single Cell Tumor Immune Profiling
summary: Single-cell and spatial readouts now pair immune cell states with TCR and BCR repertoires to relate those states to therapeutic outcome.
synthesis: The common thread is high-dimensional profiling of immune cell states that pairs transcriptomic readouts with TCR or BCR repertoire data, spatial context, or protein measurements to relate cell states to therapeutic outcome. TSTScope integrates scRNA-seq with TCR sequencing to identify functional tumor-specific T cell states predictive of immunotherapy response, and a gastric cancer study links CD8+ T cell heterogeneity to checkpoint blockade response. In melanoma, tumor-infiltrating B cells follow interferon-rich trajectories aligned with immunotherapy. What is new is methodological: scXpand detects pan-cancer T cell clonal expansion from scRNA-seq without paired TCR sequencing, and Stereo-XCR-seq recovers TCR and BCR sequences from spatial transcriptome cDNA libraries, revealing ectopic GC-like niches in lung adenocarcinoma. Other items extend comparable approaches to non-malignant immune disease, while the sialylation study examines how naive T cell glycosylation restrains bispecific engager-mediated antitumor immunity.
